purpose: Carry the execution-scope half of the S1/S2 successor authority: the FINAL path ceilings for both lanes after the repairs in the companion ODS addendum, the exact route-topology regression S2 must install, the parallelism proof, and the S1 product semantics that remain frozen verbatim. It changes no product code, no schema and no test.
scope_note: AMENDS BY ADDITION ONLY. Every grant, prohibition, product semantic and security invariant frozen by MULTI_ORG_S1_S2_EXECUTION_SCOPE_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json remains in force byte-unchanged. This amendment adds the paths that document provably could not be exercised without, corrects one measurement gap in its companion's migration reasoning, and restates the frozen semantics so an implementing mission needs no third artifact. It reopens no adjudicated product decision.

FINAL_SCOPE_CLASSIFICATION.why_classified: The audit finding this remediation closes was a SCOPE finding, so the ceiling is restated by CLASS rather than as one undifferentiated list. A path's class determines what authorises it and what the implementing mission may do to it. Conflating the classes is how the pre-remediation ceiling came to omit five mechanically forced paths.

CLASS_1_PROTECTED_PATTERNS.authorised_by: A resolved protected grant (HPO-ODS-W2-20 and HPO-ODS-W2-21 respectively) AND an ordinary --allow entry covering the same path. Both remain mandatory; neither alone suffices.
CLASS_1_PROTECTED_PATTERNS.narrowness: UNCHANGED BY THIS REMEDIATION. Neither pattern is broadened. No db/prepared/** grant of any width is created.

CLASS_2_UNPROTECTED_LITERAL_FILES.authorised_by: An ordinary --allow entry alone. No protected grant is required or permitted for them.
CLASS_2_UNPROTECTED_LITERAL_FILES.not_existing_product_tests: tests/ods/ods-scope.test.ts is an ODS-native governance control over the gate itself, authorised by an ordinary ODS path grant (adjudicated in the companion addendum FUNCTION_A). tests/tenancy/s1-founder-traceability.test.ts and tests/postgres/s1-founder-cardinality.pg.test.ts are files S1 CREATES, so no existing-test instruction can apply to them.

CLASS_3_EXISTING_TEST_HOSTS.authorised_by: An ordinary --allow entry AND the narrow per-host existing-test instruction issued in EXISTING_TEST_INSTRUCTIONS below, restated in the companion addendum FUNCTION_D and FUNCTION_F. The --allow entry ALONE is NOT sufficient for these five.

S2_ROUTE_TOPOLOGY_DECISION.RATIFIED: The selected-organization selector remains an explicit PRE-ORGANIZATION route at app/(authenticated)/app/organizations/select/*.
S2_ROUTE_TOPOLOGY_DECISION.not_relocated: It is NOT moved beneath app/app/**. Requiring organization scope in order to reach the organization selector is circular: app/app/layout.tsx calls requireOrganizationAccess(), which redirects a user without an organization to onboarding, so a selector placed there could never be reached by the only users who need it. This is the same cycle closed historically by commit 65ab17d.
S2_ROUTE_TOPOLOGY_DECISION.the_regression_evolves_deliberately: The existing route-security control is made STRICTER rather than widened. Widening is the failure mode this decision exists to avoid.
S2_ROUTE_TOPOLOGY_DECISION.control_replaced: The control currently at :155, 'carves out EXACTLY one route - every other /app/* page stays gated', whose sweep at :167 reads only the FIRST level of directory names beneath each app/(group)/app/ and asserts ['onboarding'] at :172.
S2_ROUTE_TOPOLOGY_DECISION.why_it_must_change: MECHANICAL, NOT DISCRETIONARY. Creating app/(authenticated)/app/organizations/select/page.tsx makes the swept set ['onboarding','organizations'], which fails the exact-equality assertion. S2 cannot land without touching this control.

EXACT_RULE_AUTHORIZED.shape: RECURSIVE ROUTE-PATH ENUMERATION. For each route group directory app/(<group>)/, if app/(<group>)/app/ exists, walk it recursively; every directory containing a route-serving file contributes its path RELATIVE to that app/ root, joined with '/'. Assert the deduplicated sorted set equals the exact declared carve-out list.
EXACT_RULE_AUTHORIZED.route_file_measurement_obligation: BINDING. The S2 mission MUST re-measure the repository's actual route-file conventions at its own head and use the set it measures. Omitting a name the repository DOES use would silently un-gate a route - the precise failure this control exists to prevent. Including a name it does not use is inert. MEASURED at INTEGRATION_SHA: the only route-serving file beneath any app/(group)/app/ tree is app/(authenticated)/app/onboarding/page.tsx.
EXACT_RULE_AUTHORIZED.explicitly_not_authorized: ['onboarding','organizations']. A top-level-directory form would silently authorize EVERY future app/(authenticated)/app/organizations/** route - create, [id], settings and any successor - none of which has been adjudicated as a pre-organization surface. This is expectation broadening, which the ODS existing-test adjustment class forbids.

BINDING_STRICTNESS_PROOF.obligation: The replacement must be proven STRICTLY STRONGER than the control it replaces, in both directions, BEFORE it is accepted. A replacement that is merely DIFFERENT, or that trades one blind spot for another, is gate weakening and is a STOP.

required_rows.significance: IDENTICAL VERDICT. Proves the replacement is not repairing a currently-failing control and introduces no regression on today's tree.
The authorized carve-out, and only it, is admitted.

COMMON_BINDING_RULES.no_weakening: No exact equality may be converted to a lower bound, a range, a >= comparison, a computed expression that cannot fail, a .skip, a .todo or a deletion. Advancing a pin changes WHICH exact value it demands; it never changes WHETHER it demands one.

A1_STATUS_DISPOSITION.why_it_is_mechanically_forced: MEASURED. scripts/a1-status.ts derives the artefact from artifacts/hosted-a1-corroboration.json TOGETHER WITH the live baseline manifest, and its chainPlan message counts the baseline units the recorded observation lacks - at INTEGRATION_SHA, 'refused: 28 baseline unit(s) missing, starting with 0040_governed_model_registry.sql'. Appending one baseline unit that the recorded staging observation does not contain deterministically changes that count to 29. pnpm a1:status:verify compares the on-disk bytes against a freshly serialised status and FAILS on any difference.
A1_STATUS_DISPOSITION.regeneration_is_offline: MEASURED FROM SOURCE. scripts/a1-status.ts reads with readFileSync and constructs no database client. Regeneration is a pure recomputation over the RECORDED corroboration plus the live manifest, and needs no live database, no credentials and no staging access. Its write mode REFUSES outright when the corroboration artefact is absent, so it cannot fabricate a verdict from nothing.
A1_STATUS_DISPOSITION.MANDATORY_REGENERATION: BINDING. The implementing mission MUST regenerate this artefact with the repository-native generator pnpm a1:status:write, and MUST confirm with pnpm a1:status:verify. It MUST NEVER be hand-edited. Its own first field reads 'do not hand-edit; this file is derived from the corroboration'; a hand edit would assert a verdict the recorded corroboration does not support.

NOT_HISTORICAL_CLOSURE_EVIDENCE.binding: This artefact is CURRENT-STATE evidence - what the A1 contract computes over the recorded corroboration AS OF NOW. It is NOT historical closure evidence and NOT a sealed or certified artefact. Regenerating it is the OPPOSITE of historical evidence rewriting: leaving it stale is what would misreport the current state.
NOT_HISTORICAL_CLOSURE_EVIDENCE.the_distinction_that_matters: A historical closure artefact records what was true at a past checkpoint and is immutable. A current-state generated artefact records what the contract computes today and is REQUIRED to move when its inputs move. Conflating the two is what produces both failure modes - frozen files edited, and live files left stale.
NOT_HISTORICAL_CLOSURE_EVIDENCE.corroboration_is_NOT_authorised: artifacts/hosted-a1-corroboration.json - the RECORDED PROBE OUTPUT this status derives from - falls in the FIRST category and is NOT an authorised path. It is not in the S1 ceiling and S1 must not touch it. Only the DERIVED status file is authorised. Editing the corroboration would alter the recorded observation itself, which is exactly the historical rewrite this disposition forbids.

A1_STATUS_DISPOSITION.verifier_not_a_test_host: PRECISE, AND THE REASON THIS IS NOT LISTED AS AN EXISTING TEST HOST. pnpm a1:status:verify is a repository-native CLI verifier, not a vitest spec. No file under tests/ asserts this artefact's freshness. It is therefore classified as a generated artefact governed by generator discipline, and NO existing-test instruction is issued for it. A mission that looked only for failing vitest specs would never discover this obligation.

CHECKPOINT_B0_DISPOSITION.verdict: NOT REQUIRED FOR S1. NOT AUTHORISED. NOT TO BE ADDED TO THE CEILING.
CHECKPOINT_B0_DISPOSITION.status: RECORDED NEGATIVE FINDING. This entry exists so a future reader does not 'complete' the S1 ceiling by importing a consequence that does not apply to it.
CHECKPOINT_B0_DISPOSITION.why_not: S1 ADDS COLUMNS TO AN EXISTING TABLE AND CREATES NO TABLE. organizations.founded_by and organizations.founding_provenance are added to the pre-existing organizations relation.
CHECKPOINT_B0_DISPOSITION.machine_derivation: PROVEN FROM SOURCE rather than asserted. scripts/b0-observation-sql.ts:30 builds the probe as buildB0ObservationSql(deriveExpectedBaselineState(read).tables) - the probe is TABLE-SCOPED. db/hosted/baseline-postconditions.ts:164 populates that set with a loop over facts.tablesCreated, so it is filled from CREATE TABLE facts ONLY. A migration whose DDL is ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN contributes no member to tablesCreated, the derived table set is therefore unchanged, and the generated probe is byte-identical.
CHECKPOINT_B0_DISPOSITION.machine_confirmation: pnpm b0:observation:verify was run at INTEGRATION_SHA and reported 'verification OK - the probe regenerates byte-identically from the corpus'. The implementing mission MUST re-run it after adding S1's unit and MUST obtain the same byte-identical result. That re-run is the confirmation; this reasoning is not a substitute for it.
CHECKPOINT_B0_DISPOSITION.conditional_not_absolute: BINDING HONESTY QUALIFIER. This negative holds BECAUSE S1's frozen semantics create no table. It is CONDITIONAL on that, not unconditional. If the S1 implementing mission finds itself writing a CREATE TABLE, it has departed from FROZEN_S1_SEMANTICS, and the correct response is STOP_FOR_AUTHORITY_DELTA - never to quietly add checkpoint-b0 to the ceiling and continue.
CHECKPOINT_B0_DISPOSITION.DO_NOT_IMPORT_CE1s_CONSEQUENCE: EXPLICIT. The CommercialAccount CE-1 lane DID require db/prepared/checkpoint-b0/observation.sql, because its migration CREATED A TABLE and therefore changed deriveExpectedBaselineState().tables. That consequence is specific to table creation and MUST NOT be imported into S1 by analogy. Two lanes sharing the phrase 'ordinary migration' do not thereby share this consequence, and the difference is measurable rather than a matter of judgement.
CHECKPOINT_B0_DISPOSITION.second_negative_control: MEASURED. Even a mission that wrongly concluded checkpoint-b0 were needed would not be able to reach it under this authority: db/prepared/checkpoint-b0/observation.sql is PROTECTED under DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERNS entry db/prepared/**, and matchesAnyPattern('db/prepared/checkpoint-b0/observation.sql', ['db/prepared/journal/**']) evaluates to FALSE. DETERMINISTIC_BASELINE_GROWTH.status: FROZEN BY THE BR REMEDIATION. This block is the CONTROLLING disposition for every count pin that one appended baseline unit invalidates. It replaces the pre-remediation KNOWN_TEST_CONDITIONS_CARRIED block, whose text is preserved verbatim below for audit continuity and is WITHDRAWN as guidance.

DOCTRINE.rule: DETERMINISTIC_BASELINE_GROWTH -> REGENERATE, or ADVANCE THE EXACT GOVERNED COUNT PIN -> TARGET FULL GREEN.
DOCTRINE.binding: A pin that is stale because the baseline deterministically grew is a pin that MUST BE ADVANCED. It is not a known condition, it is not an accepted failure, and it is not a candidate for registration as one. The S1 exit target is FULL GREEN on every host enumerated in EXISTING_TEST_INSTRUCTIONS, with every generated artefact regenerated by its own generator and confirmed by its own verifier.
DOCTRINE.no_new_KTC: PROHIBITED. The S1 implementing mission MUST NOT create KTC-S1-anything, nor any other new known-test-condition entry, for baseline-growth staleness. Registering a deterministic, mechanically repairable, fully specified drift as a known condition converts a bounded repair into permanent accepted debt, and hides precisely the class of failure this authority exists to force into the open.
DOCTRINE.why_this_is_not_gate_weakening: Advancing an exact pin from 78 to a MEASURED 79 leaves it an exact pin: the control still fails on any drift that was not measured. What WOULD be gate weakening is converting it to a lower bound, a range, a computed expression that cannot fail, or a registered exemption - and all four are prohibited by COMMON_BINDING_RULES.no_weakening.

WHAT_THE_TWO_KTCs_DO_STILL_COVER.KTC-HOSTED-BASELINE-REHEARSAL-STALE-01: REMAINS VALID AS A HISTORICAL AND CURRENT CONDITION, ON ITS OWN TERMS ONLY. Registered in docs/ops/ods/KNOWN_TEST_CONDITIONS_v1.0.0.json. It covers the REHEARSAL DIGEST going stale - the pinned artefact recording that a rehearsal ran against a PREVIOUS manifest. That is genuinely not repairable by editing a number, because the repair is running pnpm baseline:rehearsal:local, which requires an environment the authority lane does not have.
WHAT_THE_TWO_KTCs_DO_STILL_COVER.KTC-HOSTED-BASELINE-REHEARSAL-STALE-02: REMAINS VALID on the same terms. Same underlying cause, separate test_id, separate failure signature.
WHAT_THE_TWO_KTCs_DO_STILL_COVER.the_conflation_that_was_corrected: MATERIAL. The rehearsal digest and the baseline COUNT PINS live in the same two files but are different failures with different repairs. The two registered conditions cover the DIGEST. They never covered the COUNTS. The pre-remediation candidate reasoned from 'a registered condition exists in this file' to 'this file must not be edited', which does not follow, and which is exactly what left four mechanically forced pins outside the S1 ceiling.
WHAT_THE_TWO_KTCs_DO_STILL_COVER.same_condition_comparison_rule: BINDING AND UNCHANGED. A failure matches a carried condition ONLY on test_file plus test_id together, NEVER on filename alone. This is the registry's own rule, and it is precisely the rule the conflation violated: sharing a FILE with a registered condition is not matching that condition.
WHAT_THE_TWO_KTCs_DO_STILL_COVER.not_a_blanket_exemption: These two entries excuse exactly the two registered digest-staleness signatures. They excuse no other failure in those files. They do NOT excuse a stale evidence.unitCount pin, a stale evidence.superuserFreeUnits pin, a stale manifestOk gate literal, or a stale firstProvisioning.steps.length literal - each of which is a NEW, unregistered failure signature.
WHAT_THE_TWO_KTCs_DO_STILL_COVER.and_they_authorise_no_edit_by_themselves: A known condition states which failures are ACCEPTED. It is never itself a path grant, and never itself a path prohibition. The four forced literals in those two files are editable because EXISTING_TEST_INSTRUCTIONS HOST_4 and HOST_5 authorise them - not because a condition happens to be registered nearby.

JOURNAL_CONSEQUENCE.grant: db/prepared/journal/** - PRESERVED EXACTLY. Declared by HPO-ODS-W2-21. Neither broadened nor narrowed by the BR remediation.
JOURNAL_CONSEQUENCE.why_the_pattern_is_load_bearing: MACHINE-PROVEN, RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY AT INTEGRATION_SHA. db/hosted/baseline-journal-wrapper.ts:211 emits each wrapper's header as a GENERATED - DO NOT EDIT line carrying 'Unit <ordinal>/<BASELINE_UNITS.length>: <unit id>'. The DENOMINATOR is the live baseline cardinality, interpolated at generation time. The live wrapper db/prepared/journal/078_0065_fib_sensitivity_model.sql carries 'Unit 78/78' in its own bytes.
JOURNAL_CONSEQUENCE.the_consequence: ONE appended baseline unit therefore does TWO things at once. It CREATES one new wrapper, and it REWRITES THE DENOMINATOR IN EVERY EXISTING WRAPPER. At INTEGRATION_SHA that is 79 files regenerated, measured by pnpm journal:verify reporting 'verification OK - all 79 wrappers regenerate byte-identically'.
JOURNAL_CONSEQUENCE.why_no_exact_file_list_may_be_frozen: BINDING. Because the change set is 'every existing wrapper, plus one new one', an exact frozen file list would be wrong the moment it was written and would fail closed against the generator's own output. The PATTERN is the only correct form. This is the affirmative reason db/prepared/journal/** is a pattern grant rather than an enumeration, and it is why the pattern MUST NOT be replaced by a file list during implementation.
JOURNAL_CONSEQUENCE.MANDATORY: Wrappers are GENERATED. The implementing mission MUST regenerate them with the generator and MUST confirm with the verifier. Hand-editing a wrapper is a STOP. scripts/baseline-operator-runner.ts independently refuses a wrapper that does not carry the journal append, so a hand-written wrapper fails a second, unrelated gate as well.
JOURNAL_CONSEQUENCE.narrowness_preserved: The pattern remains a STRICT SUBSET of db/prepared/**. Re-proven at INTEGRATION_SHA with the gate's own matcher in two directions: matchesAnyPattern('db/prepared/stella_0010_organization_bootstrap_capability.sql', ['db/prepared/journal/**']) is FALSE, and matchesAnyPattern('db/prepared/checkpoint-b0/observation.sql', ['db/prepared/journal/**']) is FALSE.
